title: Flat opcycles from universal tensor exactness on a ringed site
statement: Let $\mathcal C$ be a small site and $\mathcal O$ a sheaf of commutative rings. Let $P^\bullet$ be a cochain complex of sheaves of $\mathcal O$-modules [def-pc-cochain-complex-modules] whose terms are flat [def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules]. Fix an integer $n$. If for every sheaf of $\mathcal O$-modules $N$ the total tensor complex $\operatorname{Tot}(N\otimes_{\mathcal O}P^\bullet)$ [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves] is exact in degree $n-1$ [def-pc-acyclic-complex-modules], then the opcycle sheaf $Q^n=P^n/\operatorname{im}(d^{n-1}:P^{n-1}\to P^n)$ (the cokernel in the abelian category [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]) is flat over $\mathcal O$ [def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules].

source.place: Tag 08G0 (sites-cohomology-lemma-last-one-flat), proof, cokernel/Tor argument; agent-written generalization to universal ordinary-tensor exactness, justified by the complete local diagram chase in report.md, not by assuming the source boundedness or Tor-amplitude hypotheses.

proof.text: Put $B=P^{n-1}$, $D=P^n$, $R=P^{n-2}$, $e=d^{n-2}:R\to B$, $d=d^{n-1}:B\to D$, and $q:D\to Q=\operatorname{coker}d$. Thus $de=0$ and $qd=0$. Regard each test module $N$ as a complex concentrated in degree zero. The total tensor complex in the hypothesis has the single summand $N\otimes P^j$ in degree $j$, with differential $1_N\otimes d^j$ (the other differential is zero). The symmetry from the tensor-closed node identifies this with $P^j\otimes N$, naturally and compatibly with differentials. Consequently $R\otimes N\xrightarrow{e_N}B\otimes N\xrightarrow{d_N}D\otimes N$ is exact in the middle for every $N$. Here $e_N=e\otimes1_N$ and similarly for $d_N,q_N$.

source.place: Tag 08G0 (lemma-last-one-flat), first displayed tensor sequence; direct specialization to degree-zero test complexes

proof.text: Tensoring with any fixed module preserves cokernels: by the natural tensor–Hom bijection, a map out of $N\otimes D$ annihilating $1_N\otimes d$ corresponds precisely to a map $D\to\mathcal Hom(N,-)$ annihilating $d$, which factors uniquely through $q$. Applying the bijection back gives the unique factorization through $1_N\otimes q$. Symmetry gives the same assertion in the other variable. Hence $B\otimes N\xrightarrow{d_N}D\otimes N\xrightarrow{q_N}Q\otimes N\to0$ is exact for every $N$, and tensoring any epimorphism is again an epimorphism: an epimorphism in an abelian category is the cokernel of its kernel. This is right exactness, with no flatness requirement on the fixed tensor factor.

We will use exactness on local sections, rather than exactness on all sections over an object. For an exact sequence $X\xrightarrow{f}Y\xrightarrow{g}Z$, exactness means $\operatorname{im}f=\ker g$. Thus the induced map $X\to\ker g$ is epic; forgetting module structure preserves this epimorphism by the exact forgetful-functor node. The abelian-sheaf epimorphism node supplies local lifts of every section of $\ker g$. Kernels are sectionwise by the module-category node, so every section $y$ killed by $g$ locally equals $f(x)$. The same epimorphism node supplies local lifts for any module epimorphism. These implications apply over every object and after every restriction; successive covering refinements are composed using the site covering axioms. Monomorphisms of module sheaves are injective on sections because their sectionwise kernel is zero.

source.place: Tag 03DA (lemma-abelian), exact forgetful functor; Tag 03CN (lemma-abelian-abelian), parts (2), (3), (5), (6)

proof.text: Fix an arbitrary short exact sequence $0\to N_1\xrightarrow{i}N_2\xrightarrow{p}N_3\to0$ and an object $V$. Write $X_i=1_X\otimes i$ and $X_p=1_X\otimes p$. Let $x\in(Q\otimes N_1)(V)$ satisfy $Q_i(x)=0$. Since $q_{N_1}$ is epic by step 2, locally lift $x$ to $y\in(D\otimes N_1)(V)$. Naturality gives $q_{N_2}(D_i y)=Q_i(q_{N_1}y)=0$. Exactness of the cokernel sequence of step 2 and the local criterion of step 3 give, after another covering refinement, $z\in(B\otimes N_2)(V)$ with $d_{N_2}z=D_i y$. All letters henceforth denote these restricted sections; no global lift is claimed.

source.place: Tag 08G0 (lemma-last-one-flat), cokernel-flatness argument; agent expansion by local diagram chase

proof.text: The section $B_p z$ is a cycle: $d_{N_3}(B_p z)=D_p(d_{N_2}z)=D_pD_i y=0$, because $pi=0$. Step 1 applied to $N_3$ and the local criterion give a local section $w\in(R\otimes N_3)(V)$ with $e_{N_3}w=B_pz$. Tensoring the epimorphism $p$ with $R$ is epic by step 2, even without using flatness of $R$. Locally lift $w$ to $\widetilde w\in(R\otimes N_2)(V)$. Set $z_0=z-e_{N_2}\widetilde w$. Then $B_pz_0=B_pz-e_{N_3}R_p\widetilde w=0$, whereas $d_{N_2}z_0=d_{N_2}z$ since $de=0$.

source.place: Tag 08G0 (lemma-last-one-flat), tensor exactness in degree n-1; agent expansion of the obstruction and boundary correction

proof.text: Flatness of $B=P^{n-1}$, by its defining exactness property, makes $0\to B\otimes N_1\xrightarrow{B_i}B\otimes N_2\xrightarrow{B_p}B\otimes N_3\to0$ exact. Thus the local criterion supplies $v\in(B\otimes N_1)(V)$ with $B_i v=z_0$. Naturality and the correction identity give $D_i(d_{N_1}v)=d_{N_2}B_i v=d_{N_2}z_0=d_{N_2}z=D_i y$. Flatness of $D=P^n$ makes $D_i$ monic and therefore sectionwise injective; hence $y=d_{N_1}v$. It follows that $x=q_{N_1}y=q_{N_1}d_{N_1}v=0$ on the resulting cover. The sheaf separatedness axiom gives $x=0$ on the original $V$. Since $V$ and $x$ were arbitrary, $Q_i$ is monic.

source.place: Tag 08G0 (lemma-last-one-flat), conclusion of cokernel-flatness argument; agent expansion using exactly the flat terms in degrees n-1 and n

proof.text: By step 2, $Q\otimes-$ is additive and preserves cokernels, so it sends the chosen short exact sequence to a right exact sequence. Step 6 supplies injectivity at the left, so that sequence is short exact. This holds for every short exact sequence. Write $T=Q\otimes-$. For an arbitrary sequence $A\xrightarrow{f}B\xrightarrow{g}C$ exact at $B$, set $I=\operatorname{im}f=\ker g$ and $J=\operatorname{im}g$. Factor $f$ as the epimorphism $A\to I$ followed by $I\hookrightarrow B$, and $g$ as $B\to J$ followed by $J\hookrightarrow C$. Preservation of $0\to I\to B\to J\to0$ gives $\operatorname{im}T(I\hookrightarrow B)=\ker T(B\to J)$. Right exactness makes $T(A\to I)$ epic, so $\operatorname{im}T(f)=\operatorname{im}T(I\hookrightarrow B)$. Applying the short-exact preservation already proved to $0\to J\to C\to C/J\to0$ makes $T(J\hookrightarrow C)$ monic, so $\ker T(g)=\ker T(B\to J)$. Combining these three equalities proves exactness at $T(B)$. Thus $Q\otimes-$ is exact. Tensor symmetry identifies it with $-\otimes Q$, and the flat-sheaf definition proves that $Q=Q^n$ is flat.
